full_judgment:
6. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, learned Advocate for the petitioners, appearing with Mr. Md Iftekhar Jonaed, learned Advocate, at the very outset draws out attention to Rule 8 of the said Rules and submits that under Rule-8 inclusion of two outsider members in the Evaluation Committee is mandatory, but the Evaluation Committee in question was constituted only with the officials of BTRC. Therefore, he submits, the evaluation process is void from the very beginning as the Evaluation Committee was not properly constituted. Drawing our attention to Rule 59(2) of the said Rules, he points out that although the sub-rule (2) of Rule 59 made it mandatory for the procuring entity not to publish notice for execution of procuring agreement once objection is filed before the head of the procuring entity, the BTRC admittedly published, the said notice in the newspaper on 30-3-2011 although the petitioner firm made its 1st objection before the head of procuring entity on 28-3-2011. He further argues that in view of Rule 60(5), the decision of the Review panel is final and binding on the concerned parties including BTRC, but the BTRC has been trying to avoid the compliance of the mandatory provisions of law from the very beginning, and finally by the impugned memo it refused to implement the binding decision of the Review Panel by citing some misconceived reasons. He further submits that the Review Panel though "cancelled" petitioner's review petition also cancelled the procurement process in question and asked the BTRC to start fresh procurement, and since such orders are very much within the scope of the power of the Review Panel in view of sub-rule (3) of Rule 60, the contention that the decision of the Review Panel is contradictory is misconceived and has no substance. 

 7. As against this, Mr. Murad Reza, learned Additional Attorney-General (appearing in personal capacity), appearing along with Mr. Khandaker Reza-e-Raquib, Mr. Imranul Kabir, and Mr. Mejbahur Rahman, learned Advocates for the BTRC, submits that the petitioners even do not have locus-standi to invoke writ jurisdiction, as they are not 'persons aggrieved' within the meaning of Article 102 of the Constitution. According to him since the petitioner firm will not be able to participate in the fresh tender (if any) as it conducted audit on telecom operators in the last 3 (three) years, it is not a "person aggrieved' and, as such, writ is not maintain-able. In support of his submission he refers to several decisions, namely Exparte Sidebothans [1880] 14 ChD-458, Tariq Transport vs Sargodha -Vera Bus Service, 11 DLR (SC) 140 and Bangladesh Sangbadpatra Parishad vs Government of Bangladesh, 43 DLR (AD) 126. Referring to the circular dated 2-5-2011 (Annexure-6 to the affidavit-in-opposition), he submits that since the Chairman of BTRC issued the said notification in view of Rule 59(3) certifying that it was necessary to continue with the procuring and auditing process in the public interest, the BTRC did not violate any provision of law in continuing with the procuring process even after filing of objection and appeal by the petitioners. He argues that in view of Clause-'Gha' of sub-rule (3) of Rule 60 of the said Rules, the Review Panel does not have any authority to cancel any procuring process once the procurement agreement is executed and, as such, the authority is not bound to implement the said decision of the Review Panel. Mr. Reza further argues that the petitioners have not come in clean hand as they are serving the interest of Grameen phone to sabotage the audit of respondent No. 12 on Grameen Phone as huge irregularities were found in the said audit. Finally, he submits that since the audit by respondent No. 12 has already finished to a certain extent, this Court should not interfere into it under Writ Jurisdiction as the same would cause huge loss to the BTRC and the Government. 

 13. BTRC is a statutory body constituted under sections 6 and 7 of the Bangladesh Tele Communication Act, 2001 ("the said Act") to regulate, amongst others, the functions of the telephone operators in Bangladesh. Chapter-12 of the said Act contains provisions allowing flow of information from different operators to BTRC. Thus, it is quite natural that the audit reports of different telecom operators are sent to the BTRC or collected by it on regular basis so that it can regulate the operators affairs efficiently. Therefore, it is hard to believe that the BTRC did not have information at the relevant time that respondent Nos.10 and 11 were also disqualified like the petitioner firm on account of conducting audit on telecom operators in the last three years. Rather, we are of the view that BTRC willfully waived the said disqualification in clear violation of the terms of the tender notice. Further, just because the petitioner firm will not be able to participate in the fresh tender because of the said disqualification clause in the tender notice, it should not be disentitled to challenge the irregularity/illegality allegedly committed by the BTRC in the tender process in question. We do not know what terms and conditions might there be in the fresh notice to be published by the BTRC inviting tender. They might or might not keep the said disqualification clause in the fresh tender notice. Therefore, we should not refuse audience to the petitioners on mere hypothesis. 

 18. The highhandedness of the BTRC did not end there. Admittedly, the petitioner firm filed its first objection before the head of the procuring entity on 28-3-2010 (Annexure-E to the writ petition), but the BTRC published notification of awarding contract in favour of respondent No. 10 & 12 in the Daily Star on 30-3-2011 in view of Rule-37, which is a clear violation of Rule 59(2)- as reproduced below:— 

 19. This sub-rule (2) of Rule-59 provides that once an objection is filed before the procuring entity, the notification of awarding contract shall not be published until the said objection is finally disposed of. This bar under sub rule-(2) is a clear bar providing no exceptions to it unlike sub-rule-(1) read with sub-rule-(3) of Rule 59 where-in an exception has been provided for proceeding with the notification of awarding contract if a certificate of public interest is issued by the head of procuring entity. No such exception has been provided to the provisions of sub-rule-(2) of Rule-59, which is an independent provision. However, it appears that not only the notification of awarding contract has been published pending such objection, the BTRC even executed formal agreement with respondent No. 12 on 5-4-2011 (Annexure-4 to the affidavit-in-opposition) and continued such violation thereafter. Again, when an interim request/order was sent by the CPTU to the BTRC on 24-4-2011 (Annexure-H to the writ petition) in view of Rule 59(1), the BTRC defied the same and continued to execute another formal agreement with respondent No. 11 on 26-4-2011(Annexure-5 to the Affidavit-in-opposition).
